analysis.answer: Current law makes possession of any amount of cannabis a misdemeanor punishable by up to 90 days in jail. The measure changes this by allowing adults 21 or older to possess up to one ounce of cannabis, explicitly declaring it is no longer an offense.

Law enforcement will no longer arrest or cite adults for possessing small amounts of cannabis, and courts and jails will see fewer minor possession cases. Individuals 21 and older may possess cannabis more openly.

The measure addresses the criminalization of small-scale cannabis possession and the resulting risk of incarceration. The mechanism reaches this by explicitly legalizing possession of up to one ounce for adults and removing it as a criminal offense.
Individuals 21 and older gain the discretion to legally possess small amounts of cannabis. Police and prosecutors lose the power to arrest, charge, and penalize individuals for this action.

The broader impacts of decriminalizing cannabis are disputed. Some researchers find it significantly reduces systemic criminal justice costs and mitigates disparities in enforcement, while others argue it can lead to increased substance use disorders and associated public health costs.
